question: What is VIDYADAAN?
answer: VIDYADAAN connects government schools with NGOs and donors. Schools post the infrastructure they need (for example classrooms, toilets, a library or a computer lab). The VIDYADAAN team checks every school and every project before NGOs and donors can see it. NGOs fund parts of a project and pay the school, and donors give online through Razorpay. Each project shows how much has been raised.

question: How do I create an account?
answer: Open Join (the Get started button), choose School, NGO or Donor, and fill in the form with the required documents: schools upload a registration certificate and the principal's ID proof, NGOs a registration certificate and PAN card, and donors a PAN card. Every new account is checked by the VIDYADAAN team, and you can sign in once it is approved.

question: Why can't I sign in to my account?
answer: First check that you are on the right portal (School, NGO, Donor or Admin) and that the email and password are correct. New accounts can't sign in until the VIDYADAAN team approves them; the sign-in page tells you if your account is still pending or was rejected, and shows the reason. If you forgot your password, use Forgot password on the sign-in page.

question: How do I reset my password?
answer: On any sign-in page, choose Forgot password and enter your account's email address. VIDYADAAN emails you a reset link that works once and expires after 15 minutes. If the email doesn't arrive within a few minutes, check your Spam folder. For security, the page shows the same message whether or not an account exists for that email.

question: Can I sign in with Google?
answer: Yes, if Sign in with Google is shown on the sign-in page. It signs you in to the VIDYADAAN account that uses the same email address. When an existing account is linked to Google for the first time, its old password is removed and other devices are signed out; you can set a password again with Forgot password.

question: What does Remember me do?
answer: Remember me keeps you signed in on that device for 30 days. Without it, you are signed out when you close the browser. Don't use Remember me on a shared computer.
keywords: remember me,stay signed in,keep me logged in,session

question: Is my payment information safe?
answer: Online payments are made on Razorpay's own secure checkout. VIDYADAAN never sees or stores your card number, CVV, UPI PIN or bank login. VIDYADAAN only keeps the amount, what it was for, the time, and Razorpay's order and payment IDs.

question: What is the refund policy?
answer: A confirmed online payment is refunded only if something went wrong: you were charged twice, charged a different amount from the one shown, or money left your account but VIDYADAAN never confirmed the payment. Ask within 7 days by emailing VIDYADAAN from your registered email with the Razorpay payment ID (it starts with pay_), the amount and date, and what went wrong. Approved refunds go back to the original payment method. The full policy is on the Refund Policy page.

question: How do I contact the VIDYADAAN team?
answer: Use the Contact page (the Contact Us link at the bottom of every page). It lists VIDYADAAN's email address, phone number and location. The Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and Refund Policy are linked there too.

question: Does VIDYADAAN charge any fee?
answer: No. VIDYADAAN is free to use for schools, NGOs and donors, and no fee is deducted from the money a school receives.

question: How do I create a project?
answer: On your Dashboard (or Manage Projects), choose New project. Fill in the project title, category, priority, what the problem is and how the project will help, the estimated budget in rupees, the number of students who will benefit and the expected completion date. Location and required materials are optional (without a location, your school's district is used). Then submit: the project is sent to the VIDYADAAN team for review and shows as Pending review.

question: What happens after I submit a project?
answer: Your project waits for review by the VIDYADAAN team and shows as Pending review. If it is approved, it becomes Open: NGOs and donors can see and fund it, and every active alumnus on your Alumni list gets an email about it. If the team requests changes, the project shows as Rejected with their reason (Changes requested); edit the project to fix it and it is sent for review again automatically.

question: How do I check the approval status of my project?
answer: Open Manage Projects: each project shows Pending review, Rejected (with the reason) or, once approved, its work status such as Open or In Progress. The Review updates panel on your Dashboard shows the latest decisions, and Notifications lists them too.

question: My project was rejected. What should I do?
answer: Read the reason under Changes requested on the project. Open the project, make the changes the review team asked for, and save. Editing a rejected project sends it back for review automatically, and it shows as Pending review again.

question: Can I change my project's budget?
answer: Yes, until funding starts. Once any NGO has committed to a part of the project, or any donor has given to it, the budget can no longer be changed, so the parts and donations stay correct.

question: How do I mark a project as In Progress or Completed?
answer: After your project is approved, edit it and change its Status (Open, In Progress, On Hold or Completed). The status can only be changed once the project is approved.

question: How do NGOs fund my project?
answer: Each approved project's budget is split into 5 equal parts. NGOs commit to one or more free parts and then pay for them, either online through Razorpay or directly to your school's bank account or UPI. Donors can also give online. A project's Raised amount counts NGO payments your school accepted (online NGO payments count as soon as Razorpay confirms them) and donations confirmed by Razorpay.

question: How do I check and accept a payment from an NGO?
answer: When an NGO pays your school directly, it sends proof, and the payment appears under Donation History as To check (your Dashboard also shows a reminder). Check that the money has reached your bank account, then Accept it, or Reject it with a reason if it hasn't arrived. Online payments made through Razorpay show as Paid online and need nothing from you.
keywords: accept payment,check payment,payment proof,reject payment,ngo paid,donation history,to check

question: How do I add my UPI payment QR?
answer: On your Dashboard, find UPI payment QR and choose Upload QR. Upload a screenshot or photo of your school's UPI QR from PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm or BHIM; only real UPI payment QRs are accepted, and only the payment link inside it is saved, not the image. A QR for the UPI ID verified at your registration is active at once; a different UPI ID is checked by the VIDYADAAN team first. NGOs funding your projects can then scan it; donors never see it.

question: How do I add alumni?
answer: Open Alumni in the menu and choose Add alumni. Enter the former student's full name, register number and email address; the graduation year is optional. Each register number and email can be added once per school. Only your school can see your alumni list.

question: When do my alumni get emails?
answer: When the VIDYADAAN team approves one of your projects, every active alumnus on your list gets one email about it, with the project's title, problem statement, budget and a View project link. Inactive alumni get nothing. Each email goes to one person only, so no alumnus sees another's address. Nothing is sent when you create, edit or resubmit a project.
keywords: alumni email,notification,alumni notified,approved email,why no email

question: How do I stop emails to one alumnus?
answer: On the Alumni page, choose Deactivate next to that person. Inactive alumni stay on your list but receive no project emails. Choose Reactivate to include them again.

question: How do I update my school profile?
answer: Open School Profile and choose Edit profile. You can change the principal's name, phone, address, numbers of students and teachers, and the facilities. Identity details checked at registration, such as the school name and UDISE code, can't be changed there; contact the VIDYADAAN team for those. You can also add or change the school photograph.

question: How do I add my school's location on the map?
answer: Open School Profile and find Location on map. Choose Add location, then either paste a Google Maps link to your school (in Google Maps, find the school or drop a pin, tap Share and copy the link) or use your current location while you are at the school. Check the pin on the map preview, then save. Only your school and the VIDYADAAN team can see it.

question: How do I download my school's report?
answer: Open Reports and choose Download CSV (for a spreadsheet) or Download Word (for a document). The report card includes your projects, their review and funding status, and the payments NGOs made.

question: How do I add project photos?
answer: Open Gallery and add a photo to one of your projects, choosing its stage (Before, In progress or Completed) and an optional caption. Photos can be JPG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB, and they are private to your school and the VIDYADAAN team.

question: Can my school sign in with its UDISE code?
answer: Yes. On the School sign-in page you can enter either the school's registered email address or its 11-digit UDISE code, with your password.

question: How do I find school needs to fund?
answer: Open School Needs. It lists projects the VIDYADAAN team has approved, with the school's name and place, the budget and how many parts are still free. Open a need to see the full problem statement, students benefiting, timeline and materials.

question: How do I commit funds to a project?
answer: Open the need and choose Fund. Each budget is split into 5 equal parts; choose one or more free parts (all of them is the full amount) and confirm. The parts are then reserved for your NGO and appear under Your Projects and Funding. Committing doesn't move money; you pay afterwards from Funding.

question: How do I pay for the parts I committed?
answer: Open Funding and choose Make payment on the need. Choose Pay online to pay through Razorpay: the payment counts as soon as Razorpay confirms it, and VIDYADAAN transfers the full amount to the school's verified bank account. Or choose Paid the school directly if you transferred the money yourself: the school's bank details (and its UPI QR, if it has an approved one) are shown there, and you send proof for the school to accept.

question: How do I submit payment proof?
answer: In Funding, choose Make payment, then Paid the school directly. Choose the parts the payment covers, the payment method, the reference number (for example the UTR), the date you paid, an optional note, and upload the proof as an image or PDF up to 5 MB. Send it; the school checks its bank account and accepts or rejects the payment.

question: The school rejected my payment. What now?
answer: The school's reason is shown with the payment in Funding. Check the payment with your bank, then make the payment again from Make payment with the correct details and proof. The parts stay reserved for your NGO.

question: What does Refund due mean on my online payment?
answer: Refund due means you paid parts online that had already been paid another way in the meantime. VIDYADAAN doesn't count that payment and refunds it to your original payment method.
keywords: refund due,double payment,already paid,online payment refund

question: How do I withdraw a commitment?
answer: Open Funding and choose Withdraw on the need. Only parts you haven't paid for are freed for other NGOs; parts with a payment waiting for the school, or already received, stay with your NGO.

question: How do I add volunteers?
answer: Open Volunteers and choose Add volunteer. Enter the person's name and role; the phone number is optional. You can assign them to one of the school needs your NGO is funding. You can edit or remove volunteers at any time.

question: How do I download my NGO's report?
answer: Open Reports in the menu and choose Download CSV or Download Word. The report card lists the school needs you fund (with your parts and where their money stands), every payment you made, and your volunteers.

question: Where can I see a school's bank details?
answer: Only after your NGO has committed to one of that school's needs: open Funding, choose Make payment, then Paid the school directly. Bank details are never shown to donors.
keywords: bank details,account number,ifsc,upi id,where to pay

question: How do I donate to a project?
answer: Open School Needs on your Dashboard and choose Donate on a need (or Support this project on its public page). Enter an amount between ₹10 and ₹5,00,000, then pay on Razorpay by UPI, card, net banking or another method. Your donation is confirmed only after the server verifies the payment with Razorpay, and then the need's Raised amount goes up.

question: What does Payment received but confirmation is still pending mean?
answer: Razorpay returned your payment, but VIDYADAAN couldn't confirm it with the server yet. Don't pay again. Use Check again after a moment; the payment is recorded only once, however often it is checked. If it still can't be confirmed, contact VIDYADAAN with your payment ID.

question: I closed the Razorpay window. Was I charged?
answer: No. If you close the Razorpay window before paying, nothing is charged and no donation is recorded. You can try again with the same amount.

question: How do I understand a project's funding progress?
answer: Each need shows Raised and the budget, with a progress bar and the percentage funded. Raised counts only confirmed money: NGO payments the school accepted (or that Razorpay confirmed) and donations verified with Razorpay. Fully funded means Raised has reached the budget.
keywords: funding progress,raised,progress bar,percentage,fully funded,how much funded,transparency

question: Why can't I donate the amount I want to a need?
answer: A need accepts donations only up to what is still open: its budget minus the parts NGOs have committed to and what donors have already given. If you enter more, the donation window tells you the most you can give. A need that is fully funded or completely promised by NGOs takes no more donations.
keywords: limit,maximum,can't donate,fully funded,promised by ngos,amount too high

question: Where can I see my donations?
answer: Open My Donations on your Dashboard. It lists every donation Razorpay confirmed, with the need, school, amount and payment ID; keep the payment ID as your reference. You can download the list as a report with Download CSV or Download Word.

question: What does Test mean next to a donation?
answer: VIDYADAAN currently uses Razorpay test mode. A donation marked Test was made with test keys, so no real money was charged.

question: Can schools see my name?
answer: No. Donors' names are not shared with schools. Schools see the total confirmed funding for their projects.

question: Why did I receive a project notification?
answer: Your school added you to its alumni list on VIDYADAAN. Whenever the VIDYADAAN team approves one of your school's projects, everyone on that list who is active gets one email with the project's details and a View project link.

question: How do I stop getting these emails?
answer: Ask your school to remove you from its alumni list or mark you inactive. Inactive alumni receive no project emails. The email itself doesn't have an unsubscribe link yet.
keywords: unsubscribe,stop emails,opt out,remove me,no more emails

question: What is the View project link?
answer: It opens the public page of that exact project on VIDYADAAN: the school, the problem it wants to solve, the budget and how much has been raised so far. Anyone can open it without an account.

question: How can I support my school's project?
answer: Open the project's page and choose Sign in to donate. You need a VIDYADAAN donor account: create one from Join, and you can donate once the VIDYADAAN team has approved it. Donations are paid securely on Razorpay. You can also share the project page with others.
keywords: support,donate,help school,contribute,give back,how can i help

question: Is my email address shared with other alumni?
answer: No. Each project email is sent to one person only, so no alumnus sees another's name or address. Only your school can see its alumni list.

question: Is the project genuine?
answer: Every project on VIDYADAAN was submitted by a registered school whose account the VIDYADAAN team verified, and the team reviewed the project before it was published. The project page shows the amount confirmed so far.

question: How do I approve new accounts?
answer: In the Admin dashboard, open Accounts and filter by Pending (and by type if you like). Choose Review on an account to see its registration details and open its verification documents. Then Approve account, or Reject with a reason of at least 5 characters, which the applicant sees when they try to sign in.

question: How does project approval work?
answer: Open the Projects tab. Projects waiting for review are listed first come, first served. Choose Review to see the school, the problem statement, budget, students, timeline and materials. Approve project makes it Open: NGOs and donors can see it, and the school's active alumni are emailed. Reject asks for a reason (5 to 500 characters) that the school sees; the school can edit the project, which sends it back for review.
keywords: project approval,approve project,review project,reject project,pending projects,workflow

question: Why can't I approve a project?
answer: A project can be approved only while it is waiting for review and only if its school's account is active. If the school's account is not active, the review window says so and Approve is disabled. A project that was already approved or rejected can't be decided again.
keywords: cannot approve,can't approve,approve disabled,school not active,already approved

question: How do I review a school's payment QR?
answer: Open the Payment QRs tab. A school's UPI QR needs your approval only when its UPI ID differs from the one verified at registration. Check the UPI ID and payee name, then approve it, or reject it with a reason. NGOs see a QR only once it is active.

question: How are admin accounts created?
answer: There is no public admin sign-up. Admin accounts are created, or their passwords reset, by someone with server access running npm run create-admin with the admin's email. Admins then sign in on the Admin sign-in page.

question: What happens to alumni emails when I approve a project?
answer: After approval, the project's school's active alumni are queued for one email each, and the approval message tells you how many were queued. Emails are sent in the background, so approval never waits for them; if email isn't set up or a send fails, the project stays approved and the failure is recorded.

question: Can admins change funding amounts or mark payments as paid?
answer: No. Raised amounts change only when a school accepts an NGO's payment or Razorpay confirms an online payment or donation. Admins review accounts, projects and payment QRs.
